html:
"Now You're a Sorcerer" is an interlude moved nineteen years ago, to Waymar August 1756. The city has just received two Sacred Objects from the new Gift, and an orphan apprentice librarian meets a mysterious young man who reads books as greedily as others eat bread.

Time and place

The action takes place in Waymar, the main city of Shayland County on Lake Smokey Dahl, in August 1756. (Smoky Distance) The Gift of the Gods has just arrived in Shayland. The city experienced alarming weeks: the count sharply raised taxes, the guard subdued dissatisfied artisans, and according to the rumor about the impending siege, the townspeople bought up everything edible in the bazaar in an hour. The Sunrises took almost all the Sacred Objects from the Gift, but the Origins' cairns took them from the Sunrises. (Sunsetters) Two Objects the Northern Duke Desmond Origin immediately gave to the Earl of Shayland to put them in the Cathedral of Vivian to the delight of the townspeople. On this occasion, the emperor came to the city with the prince and the capital’s entourage.

Plot

Guest at the Library Door

The orphan Mick of fifteen years, nicknamed Quick Mick, served as an apprentice to master Linen Margaret Harvey, the keeper of the Waymar City Library. (Mik) Once after sunset, Mick worked on the book "black wind" - the reception, which swamp assassins, stinging crybola, sneak up on the victim. At this time, a battered skinny boy stabbed at the door. He was shaking, then convulsions began with foam at the mouth, and he begged to give him the book, otherwise in a couple of minutes he would have a “collapse”. He called himself "light" - "not shadow, not casual, but light" - and lamented that there is no "sphere". Linen gave him the "Difficult Fate of the City on Torrey" by Master Hodgson, the story of Waymar. For the first two minutes, the guest looked at the turn, as if trying to understand the letters, and then read the book in about ten minutes. He calmed down and for an hour called all the dates and numbers from it along with the page numbers. Linen saw in this the blessing of Foremother Emilia, the creator of the alphabet. The next morning he gave the guest books again, and by the evening he had read at least three dozen.

Mick and his dream

Mick told about the guest to his friend Doug, the city guard two years older. Doug grew up with him in the same ditch: sometimes he defended Mick, and sometimes he took his alms from him. He decided that the guest is a “lordensh” who will also take away Mick’s place. Doug advised to find out whose son he is and return him to relatives for a reward, and give half the reward to him for advice.

The narrator reveals Mick's past. Mick was from the Old Port. The first five years of his life, while his parents were alive, he almost did not remember, the next five were climbing in the streets. One day, a bank guard nearly beat him to death, and Mick fainted on the steps of the reading room. Linen went out and took him as an apprentice, although Mick only knew the letter "A". Five years have passed since then. Mick read still poorly, but perfectly mastered science to please visitors and perfectly remembered where each book stands, who took it and what he said about it. Mick had a hare's lip and an insulting nickname for Guba. He began dreaming of Darkwater's sorcery because of Clarissa, the daughter of an elder of the shipping guild. She studied three times a week in the reading room and stressed never looked him in the face. For the sake of the love potion, Mick overcame two books on Darkwater magic in three months, but they were written by condescending imperial scientists, and there were no recipes there.

“Let’s say, Nathaniel.”

The guest called himself “let’s say, Nathaniel”: the real name, according to him, was too long and complex. To Mick's guess that he was fourteen, he replied, "Yes, you're right." He said strangely: about “your culture”, that in his country it is ethical to lie if the truth is inappropriate. He admitted that he was beaten twice, when he honestly called his homeland. He bribed Mika by looking him straight in the face and calling the “distortion of appearance” not worth the attention. Mick put together the signs - "light", "sphere", thirst for books, indifference to food, a distant land, for which they beat - and decided that the guest is a sorcerer from Darkwater. Nathaniel agreed, and when asked if he was a sorcerer, he first asked what Mick meant by that word.

Nathaniel's miracles Mick watched every day. He did not suffer from hunger, but he had to read at least a book at two hours, and after an hour without reading, he began to rush around the room. He woke up at an internal clock minute per minute and noticed that the five-minute hourglass went five minutes thirteen seconds. He immediately said that thirty-six by twenty-five was nine hundred, and immediately wrote out a chain of works up to a fifteen-digit number. He healed his bruises in three days and was ashamed that it had taken him so long. Linen saw in all this only the benefit of reading. Mick wrote a legend to Nathaniel: a student from Faunterra, who was traveling to his grandmother’s in the Southern Way, mistakenly boarded a boat to Waymar, was robbed and is now waiting for a response to a letter to his relatives. In return, Nathaniel promised not to forget the favor.

Guardians in the Market

On Sunday, Mick led Nathaniel to the lake bazaar to learn the capital's reprimand and shortened his name to Nathan. Nathan was helpless in the city. He was afraid of horses, because “everyone rides these... salamanders,” was horrified by open gutter ditches, spoke of “magic sewers,” called the festive decoration “a depravity,” and lectured to the constable. Through the gap at the wall of the Cathedral of Vivian friends climbed into the square, where only well-dressed citizens were allowed. There they settled behind two Imperial Guards, Sir William and Sir Claude. Sir William was outraged that the Earl of Shayland, "the son of a merchant", had come to the altar before the Lord at the festive prayer. According to him, the emperor thought to abolish the county and make it the land of the Crown, as the Duke of Almer proposed, but now this is impossible: the Shaylands were protected by the Origins themselves. (Aiden Almera)

Sir Claude noticed the surveillance and grabbed Nathan by the ear, and Mick had time to bounce. Nathan posed as a student in the Faculty of Physics and Sparkling Techniques at the University of Faunterra. Sir William’s brother studied at this faculty, but Nathan described the faculty coat of arms, the campus and the fountain, which turns off when the lights are lit, all this he read at night in the history of the University. He's been released. Nathan was touched that Mick did not escape, but remained to rescue him.

Objects in the Cathedral

Nathan admitted that he came "magic way" through the portal. He was going to a "very far away" place, and at Mick's prompting - the Bear Fang - reluctantly agreed. The portal threw him into the Smokey Dahl, and he barely floated out. In a month or two, Nathan hoped, other sorcerers would open a portal behind him; he himself could do nothing without a sphere. Mick took an oath from him to give him magical power if he helped, and took him to the cathedral of Vivian. To pass without a queue, Mick shrugged the lady at the entrance, protruding a hare's lip.

There were two objects on the altar. The Light Sphere consisted of two glass rings embedded one in the other, and the inner was floating in the air. (Radiant Sphere) The second item was a transparent rod with a shoulder in silvery drops. Seeing the Objects, Nathan turned pale in horror. He extended his hands to the Sphere, but the priest forbade touching. When an inch remained to the palms, a wave of weak light ran through the outer ring. Sterzhen Nathan called “cleaner” (“Why do you...”). The priest corrected him: The object is called the Rose of Happiness, and the highest chapter can still rename it. The guards in the cathedral Nathan counted thirty-nine. Sorokov was Doug, standing behind the column: he stopped Mick and asked about the “lordenysh-scribe”.

The Seed of Magic Power

At night, Mick found Nathan in tears over the old manuscript register of Sacred Objects. The chance that he will be taken back, Nathan estimated at “one whole two-tenths of a percent.” Mick again demanded magic power. Nathan took an oath from him once to fulfill one order, wiped his face with wet paper and pressed it, salty with tears, to Mick's tongue for a minute. Mika took the cold to the bone, and Nathan burned the rest of the paper in the lamp.

“You are the seed of magic. It will grow soon.”

For four days, Mick waited for the force to manifest, but nothing happened. Nathan now read books about the Objects, Gifts of the Gods, and Treasures of the Great Houses, and went to the cathedral every day. When Clarissa reproached Mick that he had confused the book, he answered her boldly for the first time that he had looked at the book no more than she had looked at him. Clarissa stared into his face for the first time, and Mick winked at her and left.

Betrayal

On the evening of the fourth day, Nathan warned that they would do "something in the cathedral" the next night. That night, Doug beat Mick with a truncheon and demanded half of what Mick had "poked" from the Lord, and after hitting his knee, it was already two-thirds. Mick told him everything: Nathan is a sorcerer from Darkwater, came through the portal, lost his strength and is looking for an opportunity to touch the Sphere. He was silent about the tears. Mick suggested blackmailing Nathan by handing out priests and forcing him to open a portal directly to the bank. Doug took up the idea: the new bishop is a Maximian monk who "does all the sorcery very closely", and Doug himself befriended the deacon. Mick offered to share the gold in half with Nathan, and the rest - to them for a quarter; Doug demanded a third.

The next day Nathan read a book of poems, Therese and Ballad of Ships, and told Mick to rub the crayons into the dust. He first angered the masters of Linen with the proposal to rearrange the books, and then convinced them to keep in the reading room the three best books of each section and, under this pretext, he asked the cathedral to thank Mother Emilia. In the cathedral, he asked Mick if there was any nobility, valor and mercy in the world, and freed him from the oath, saying that his idea was contrary to the laws of honor. Mick refused to be released. At the altar, Nathan read a prayer, made a spiral, and walked away. Then the inner ring of the Sphere itself turned, and the Object fell from the altar. In the turmoil, the friends hid in a niche among the marble statues, showering each other with chalk. Nathan estimated the chance of them being noticed to be below two percent. The priest did not allow the guard to be placed inside the cathedral, explaining that the Sphere needed privacy, and the captain doubled the external guard. The cathedral was locked up for the night.

Night in the Cathedral

At night, Nathan said he wanted more knowledge than strength from the Sphere. Here, Doug came out from behind the column, warning the deacon in advance. He was counting on the rank and church reward for the capture of the kidnapper of the shrine: either Nathan himself will take the Sphere, or Doug will break his bones and blow it, and then blow the horn, and a hundred monks will run away. Nathan promised him magical power: for a thousand years, no one could talk to the Objects. As proof, he announced to Micah his order to take Rosa Happiness and say two words, but at the last moment he changed his mind: Rosa gives "too much power." Instead, Mick took the Sphere and said one word, “idyan.” The outer ring shone with blue fire, the inner one wrapped up, and circles of light ran around the temple.

Doug vowed to give Nathan his uniform, helmet, baton and horn. He drank blood from the cut palm of the sorcerer, took the Rose of Happiness and pronounced "owasvotohyrp". A silver drop of glass on his palm and absorbed into his skin. Then, as if undressing, Doug stabbed Nathan in the stomach, put a blade to his throat and demanded a second word, promising quick death as a reward. Nathan whispered, "Itsic." Doug repeated it, and his body blackened, burned without fire, and turned into a skeleton covered with gray ash. The mummy smelled like abandoned conflagrations and very old books — “eternity”.

“I really didn’t want to kill anyone. Thank you for doing it yourself.”

Nathan healed a wound that left only a red scar. Mick brought the Sphere and told her "Adyin!", and a luminous disk appeared above it - a map of Lake Shayland, and then, according to Nathan, all of Polaris under the dome of the cathedral. Nathan whispered a long spell, and on the map clusters, like a dam, appeared white dots with signs, usually in or near cities. The first dense cluster was in Waymar itself. Another scattering, not far from the city, Nathan looked with pain and sadness. He then briefly inspected the clusters in the east, in the center and in the south. Mick thought the sorcerer was choosing where to go, but Nathan replied that he was "just looking for something."

The Magician's Departure

The door slammed: the monks noticed the light. Nathan extinguished the Sphere, put on Doug's uniform, and told Mick to drag the mummy into a spot of moonlight at the door. He said that the portal would only miss one thing and that things would have been different if Mick hadn't given away the secret. He then listed Mick three ways. If the truth is told, he will not be believed and will probably be tortured. If you lie that Doug was a dark sorcerer and was killed by the light power of the Sphere, Mika can be considered an accomplice. If you hide, they'll probably find him. “I was hoping for you. It’s a shame you failed.” Nathan sounded the alarm. Monks and guards burst into the cathedral and screamed in horror over the mummy, and Nathan, almost indistinguishable from the guards, ran out after the two frightened. No portal Mick did not see and no more Nathan did not meet.

The guards pulled Mick out of the niche, and one of them brought a baton. Then Mick felt that he was no longer an Orphan Mick or a Fuzzy Mick. He pointed his fingers at the guard and hissed "Yasvotohirp Itsic!" He did not know how to kill without the Object, but the guard did not know this and turned back. Mick threatened a terrible death to anyone who touched him. A monk in Maximian dress came out to him, but Mick agreed to speak only to the bishop and only if he swore that Mika would not be touched: “I am a sorcerer of great power!”

Characters

  • Mick (Strict Mick, Guba) is an orphan of fifteen years from the Old Port, an apprentice librarian who dreams of witchcraft; later, a sorcerer from A Doll on the Throne. (Mik)
  • Nathaniel (Nathan) is a mysterious young wizard who calls himself "light"; according to his agreement with Mick's guess, he is fourteen. (Navi)
  • Master Linen Margaret Harvey is the keeper of the Waymar City Library, a kind man who sheltered Mick and Nathaniel.
  • Doug is a city guard, a friend of Mick's who died from Rosa Happiness.
  • Clarissa is the daughter of an elder of the shipping guild, the subject of Mika's dreams.
  • Sir William and Sir Claude are Imperial Guards from the Emperor's entourage.

Significance in the Series

The interlude shows the appearance in Polaris of a young man who would later become known as Navi. In Humans and Gods, Navi remembers a good Waymar librarian as the first person in Polari to help him. Father David tells Erwin that the alien "initiated the boy Mick with his firstblood" and that Mick got to the church guard, and through her - to the secret order. Nineteen years later, Mick returns in "A Doll on the Throne" as the Magician - a man with a cleft lip and a stolen Object Belt who robs Shayland's banks as he dreamed in the interlude. (Mik) According to Mick and the old librarian, Nathaniel was a kind sympathetic crank. David, however, considers Nathaniel and Paul to be one man who was brutalized for ten years in Waymar prison. In Shadow of the Great Tree, Navi reveals that there was no "portal". (The Shadow of the Great Tree) There were three of them - he, Paul and Lilanne; in the crash, Lilanne died, the catapult threw Navi into the Smokey Dahl, and the "dark" Paul fell "directly into hell" and survived thanks to Eternity. In the prison of the Shaylands, Paul, and the young man from this story - "bright" Navi. There, the Light Sphere is called the “seeker”: she draws a map of Polaris, on which lights mark the places where the Objects are stored. Interlude shows for the first time the rules of the Objects: command words spoken backwards. On the same days of August 1756, the "Price of Fear" retrospection occurs in Humans and Gods, where it is said that the Origins found "something curious" in the Lodge of Dara.

Trivia

  • Command words Items are ordinary words read backwards: "idyan" - "find", "owsvotohirp" - "prepare", "itsich" - "clean". Hence the reservation of Nathan, who called Rosa Happiness a “cleaner”.
  • When asked by Nathaniel what he meant by the word "sorcerer", Mick replied: "The sorcerer is the one who has special knowledge and knows what is inaccessible to other people", and only then the guest admitted: "I am a sorcerer".
  • In the cathedral, Nathan said, "I want knowledge more than strength."
  • Unread books in the library, according to Nathan, remained five thousand four hundred and sixty-three.
